You'll need to add these same settings in the API Download Configuration. This ensures your validation credentials get passed by Chrome and the CLU app.

Once you have everything configured, you can test it out.

docs.title: Download Status Page
docs.text: From this page you can view current and pending downloads.

docs.title: Download Queue
docs.text:
Downloads are queued in the order they are received. Downloads are restricted to 3 at a time. When one download finishes, the next in the queue will start.

Once a download is started, the Filename and File Size/Downloaded fields will populate. Prior to starting, downloads currently show "N/A" for file details.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
This will show one of the following statuses:

  • queued
  • in_progress
  • retry_pending (new in v6.4)
  • error
  • complete

docs.title: Automatic Retries
docs.text:
New in v6.4

A failed download is now retried automatically up to 3 times before it's reported as failed.

Most download failures are transient — an overloaded GetComics mirror, a dropped connection, a 5xx — and would have succeeded on a second attempt a few minutes later. CLU already failed over between mirrors, but once the last mirror raised, that was the end of it and you had to notice the red row and click Retry by hand.

A failed download is now parked and re-queued 3 times, spaced 1, 5 and 15 minutes apart. The row shows the wait live:

Retrying in 4m 12s (2 of 3) — in warning colour, with the last error on hover.

While a retry is pending the row offers Cancel rather than Retry, since it's already going to run again. Clear Failed Downloads won't delete a row that's waiting to retry.

Failure notifications wait for the retries

The Download failed push notification is held back until all three retries are spent, so a notification means "this one is genuinely dead" rather than "the first mirror hiccuped" — and it tells you how many retries were burned.

A manual retry during a backoff doesn't double-download: the pending timer expires into a no-op.

Scope

Retries cover direct downloads — GetComics, Pixeldrain, MEGA, ComicBookPlus. Usenet and DC++ clients do their own retrying.

A hand-driven Retry now also keeps the download's fallback mirrors, which it used to silently drop.

docs.title: Blocked by Cloudflare
docs.text:
New in v6.4

Cloudflare-blocked downloads now say so, and offer the link that actually works.

A managed Cloudflare challenge is the one download failure CLU can't retry its way out of — no automated client can pass one. These rows previously showed a bare error with nothing explaining why, and a Retry button that could only fail again.

Now:

  • The Status column reads "Blocked by Cloudflare" in warning styling, with a hover explanation.
  • The Actions column leads with a Download manually button that opens the original GetComics page in a new tab — ahead of Retry, because Retry is pointless here.

These downloads skip the automatic retries entirely. Three more attempts would do nothing but delay the manual link you actually need by twenty minutes.

docs.title: Downloads from every source
docs.text:
The Status page shows all three download sources in one table, each with its own icon:

Source What you see Notes Direct (GetComics) Queue position, filename, size, and percentage. Downloaded by CLU itself. Usenet Live percentage, byte counts, and the client's current stage — Downloading / Verifying / Repairing / Extracting / Moving. View-only rows; SABnzbd/NZBGet does the work. Refreshed on a ~5-second cadence while active. DC++ Live percentage, stage, byte counts, and the bundle's target. View-only rows. Bundles queued directly in AirDC++ also appear, read-only — CLU never moves those. See Status & Restart Recovery.

DC++ jobs survive a restart

DC++ bundles are recorded in the database at grab time, so a container restart no longer orphans one — and a bundle that completed while CLU was down can still be imported. Failed and complete-but-not-moved rows persist until you dismiss them, deliberately. Usenet jobs are not yet covered by this. See Status & Restart Recovery.

You don't have to watch this page

As of v6.4, CLU can push a notification to Discord, Telegram, ntfy, email and 100+ other services when a download completes or fails — from all three sources. Set it up in Settings → Notifications.

docs.title: Completed Downloads
docs.text:
Downloads use the Folder Monitoring feature to process downloads. All files will saved in the WATCH directory and moved to the TARGET once they are processed.

You can adjust how files are processed in the File Settings.

docs.title: Cancel
docs.text:
Before a download starts or while in progress, you can cancel a download. Once cancelled, the details are still present until you click the "Clear Completed / Cancelled Downloads" button

Cancel actually stops the download (fixed in v6.3)

Cancellation is cooperative — the button sets a flag and the download worker has to notice it. Two providers didn't, and the old failure modes were actively misleading:

  • A cancelled Pixeldrain download ran to completion and got imported anyway, while the UI said "cancelled".
  • A cancelled GetComics download came back as Failed with a Retry button — the cancel triggered an error that then overwrote the cancelled status.

Both now check for cancellation before and during transfer, delete the partial file (which is resume state and must not survive a cancel), close the connection so the mirror stops streaming, and refuse to overwrite a cancelled status with an error.

Stopping isn't instantaneous. Granularity is bounded by chunk size, so on a slow link a cancel takes a few seconds to take effect.

docs.title: Clear Completed
docs.text:
Fixed in v6.5 — Clear Completed now clears everything

The button only ever cleared direct downloads. Usenet and DC++ rows stayed on the page reading "Complete" after you clicked it — which is precisely what made the button look broken. It now covers all three sources.

Two rows that behave differently, and deliberately so:

  • A download that finished but couldn't be filed clears as completed, not failed. The download genuinely worked; what failed afterwards was CLU finding the file — most often because the download client is running on another host and CLU can't see the path it wrote to.
  • Bundles queued directly in AirDC++ are never cleared. They aren't CLU's jobs to forget. See Status & Restart Recovery.

docs.title: Automated Downloads
docs.text:
If you are using the Metron API and the Pull List feature, CLU will attempt to auto-download all missing issues for the series on your pull list.

New in v6.5 — the sweep is visible while it runs

The scheduled sweep and Run Now now report into the header's Active Operations indicator, not just the per-series button.

A run that can last hours used to be completely invisible unless you happened to have started it from a series page. It also can't now run twice over the same scope, and queues at most 150 downloads per run — see Downloading the right comic.

docs.title: File Management
docs.text:
CLU includes a dual-pane, real-time File Manager designed for managing comic files and directories directly within your browser. You can organize folders, rename issues, split collections, manage embedded metadata, and safely trash unwanted files through an intuitive drag-and-drop interface.

Real-Time File System Access

The File Manager reads and interacts directly with your storage file system rather than relying exclusively on cached database records. Actions performed here are reflected immediately on disk.

docs.title: File Management Tools
docs.text: Feature Description Documentation Move Drag and drop files and folders between Source and Destination panels, or bundle selections into new folders. Move Rename Rename individual files inline, remove or replace text across filenames, or standardize series names. Rename Split File Deconstruct bundled multi-issue CBZ archives into standalone, single-issue CBZ files. Split File Delete & Trash Safely remove files and folders with optional soft-delete protection via the Trash Can. Delete Additional Tools Fast directory filtering, global search, recent file history, size inspections, and cover previews. Additional Features Adding Metadata Scrape metadata across providers (Metron, ComicVine, GCD, MangaDex) and generate sidecars. Adding Metadata ComicInfo.xml Options Understand search hierarchies, volume matching, and ComicInfo.xml generation. ComicInfo.xml Options

docs.title: Adding Metadata
docs.text: CLU supports multiple comic metadata providers that can be configured per library. You can search across multiple databases simultaneously in your preferred priority order when scraping and embedding metadata.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
CLU queries configured metadata providers to generate standard ComicInfo.xml metadata inside your comic archives. Providers can be assigned per library with configurable priority ordering — CLU queries providers in sequence and applies tags from the first provider that returns a valid match.

Provider Status Description Metron Metron Comic Book Database ComicVine ComicVine Cloud Database ComicVine (Local DB) Local ComicVine SQLite database (requires local setup) GCD API Grand Comics Database API GCD Grand Comics Database (requires local setup) MangaDex MangaDex Manga Database MangaUpdates MangaUpdates Database Bedetheque European Comic Database (Planned)

If you have enabled a Local Metadata Database, an additional search option appears in the File Manager to query your local SQLite cache.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Navigate to Settings > Metadata Providers to configure provider API keys, test connections, and adjust priority ordering. Save and test each provider before use — a green checkmark confirms successful API connectivity.

Make sure to enable each provider for the specific library you wish to query. See Assign Metadata Providers to Libraries for details.

docs.title: CVINFO File and Creation
docs.text:
Comic series folders can store a .cvinfo sidecar file containing ComicVine and Metron series IDs. This provides persistent series identification, ensuring future issues placed in that folder match immediately without requiring ambiguous text searches.

To create or edit a sidecar file, open the series folder in the File Manager and click the Add CVINFO button.

Enter the ComicVine ID or Metron ID for the series. CLU also creates this sidecar automatically when subscribing to a series via the Pull List or retrieving metadata for a folder.

docs.title: Automated Metadata on File Move
docs.text:
When moving files, CLU can automatically apply metadata if configured in File Settings:

  • A valid cvinfo sidecar exists in the destination directory.
  • The file does not currently contain a ComicInfo.xml file (or existing metadata was generated from basic store data and needs enrichment).

docs.title: Automated Renaming on Metadata Retrieval
docs.text: When metadata is added to an archive, CLU can automatically rename the file to match your configured Custom Rename Pattern using verified series, volume, and issue tags.

docs.title: Handling Unmatched Issue Numbers
docs.text:
When scraping metadata, CLU matches issues against the identified volume using exact issue numbering. If an issue uses non-standard numbering (such as decimal variants like 1.MU, letters like 13A, or differing numbering conventions), CLU opens an interactive issue picker displaying all issues from that volume:

Issue picker displaying available volume entries

Select the correct issue card to apply the metadata tags.

docs.title: Batch Folder Processing
docs.text: During automated folder runs, files with unmatched issue numbers are collected in the background rather than interrupting the batch. Once the main sweep finishes, you can step through and resolve any flagged near-misses sequentially.

docs.title: Match Precedence
docs.text: Exact matches from any configured provider always take priority. The manual issue picker is only presented after the entire provider cascade has been queried without an exact issue match.

docs.title: Additional Features
docs.text: The File Manager includes several built-in tools to help inspect, search, and manage your collection efficiently.

docs.title: Directory Filtering
docs.text:
For directories containing more than 25 folders, an interactive filter bar appears at the top of the list. Typing into the field immediately filters the visible folder list in real time.

Filtering Large Directory Filtered Results

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Use the search bar to locate specific comic titles, issue numbers, or series across your library storage.

When CLU starts, all files and folders are indexed into the local database for rapid query response. When files or folders are moved or renamed, the database index updates automatically.

See File Index Management for details on re-indexing. Searches span your entire library, excluding any temporary folders configured in Folder Monitoring.

docs.title: Upload Files
docs.text: You can upload comic files directly to your server by dragging and dropping them from your computer into either the Source or Destination panel of the File Manager.

docs.title: Recent Files
docs.text: Click Recent Files to view the last 100 comic files added or moved within your collection. This provides a quick way to review newly acquired downloads or recently processed files.

docs.title: File & Folder Sizes
docs.text:
To check folder metrics without slowing down list rendering, click the info icon next to any folder. CLU scans the directory on demand and returns the total file count and disk usage.

When browsing files, individual file sizes are displayed alongside each issue, making it easy to compare file editions and identify higher-resolution scans.

docs.title: View Cover, Metadata, and ComicInfo.xml
docs.text:
Click the info icon next to any comic file to open the inspector modal. This window displays the cover image, file technical properties, and any embedded ComicInfo.xml metadata.

Use the <- Prev and Next -> buttons to browse through adjacent issues in the folder.

If an issue contains invalid or outdated ComicInfo.xml data, click the icon to clear the metadata. Upon confirmation, CLU unpacks the archive, removes the XML file, and repacks the CBZ.

docs.title: Want to Read
docs.text: Select Want to Read from the actions menu on any file or folder to flag it for your personal reading list. Flagged items surface in the Want to Read carousel on your collection dashboard. In multi-user installations, this flag is personal to your user account.

docs.title: Add to Pull List
docs.text:
Select Add to Pull List from any series folder's action menu to subscribe to that series.

This runs the same identification and mapping engine used by Scan Library, but scoped to that single folder. Series sidecar files are backfilled, issue checklists are synchronized, and missing counts update in the background.

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.text:
Outcome Meaning Recommended Action already_mapped The folder is already mapped to an active series on your Pull List. No action required. applied The series was identified and mapped. Issues sync in the background. No action required. View the series in your Pull List. needs_match No matching sidecar (series.json or .cvinfo) was found. A search picker opens allowing you to search and select the correct series. conflict The series is already mapped to a different folder. CLU reports the existing path. Verify which folder is correct on the Series page. failed The mapping operation could not complete. Check App Logs for details.

Folder Scope

  • Folders must reside within a configured library path.
  • Top-level root folders (representing publishers) cannot be mapped directly to a single series.

docs.title: Generate ComicInfo.xml
docs.text: Depending on your configured metadata providers and whether you are processing a single file or an entire folder, CLU uses structured search hierarchies to find and apply comic metadata.

docs.title: Get Metadata for All Comics in a Folder
docs.text:
To fetch metadata and embed a ComicInfo.xml file across all issues in a folder, click the Fetch Metadata for All Comics in Folder button.

CLU queries configured providers using the following search hierarchy:

  1. {Series Name} ({Year}): Uses the series name and publication year extracted from the folder structure to find an exact volume match.
  2. {Series Name}: If no exact year match is found, queries for the exact series title.
  3. % {Series Name} %: If no exact title match is found, performs fuzzy keyword matching across provider records.

docs.title: Series Name (Year)
docs.text:
Searching for a structured folder like H.A.R.D. Corps (1992) matches the series and publication year directly, applying metadata tags across all issues. Any issues already containing valid metadata are skipped.

Progress is displayed in a toast notification and updates in the top navigation header, allowing you to browse elsewhere while scraping continues in the background.

docs.title: Nested Volume Folders: Series Name \ v(Year)
docs.text:
When managing multi-volume series organized into subfolders (e.g. Archer & Armstrong/v1992), CLU combines the parent directory name with the volume year to query the provider for Archer & Armstrong (1992).

If multiple potential volumes match (e.g. Archer & Armstrong (2012)), an interactive selection modal displays candidate series along with issue counts and date ranges:

Select the correct series entry to begin scraping and writing metadata.

docs.title: Get metadata for a single issue
docs.text:
When fetching metadata for an individual issue, CLU applies a targeted search hierarchy:

  1. {Series Name} {Year} {Issue Number}: Attempts to identify the exact volume and issue number directly.
  2. {Series Name} {Year}: Locates the series volume, then searches for the specific issue number within it.
  3. % {Series Name} %: Performs a keyword search across series titles, displays candidate matches, and matches the issue upon selection.

Select the matching volume and issue card to generate and write the ComicInfo.xml tag file.

docs.title: GCD API Considerations
docs.text:
When utilizing the Grand Comics Database (GCD) via its API, keep the following characteristics in mind:

  • Language Filtering: GCD catalogs international comics across numerous languages. If a search yields multiple foreign editions, use the language filter dropdown in the results modal to isolate your preferred language.
  • Result Details: Unlike ComicVine and Metron, basic GCD API search results do not always return cover art previews or publisher summaries. These fields populate once an issue is selected and downloaded.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: CLU allows you to delete individual files, entire directories, or multi-selected batches from the File Manager and Collection views.

docs.title: Deleting Files
docs.text:
To delete an individual comic file:

  1. Click the :wastebasket: (Trash) icon on the file row or select Delete from its action menu.
  2. A confirmation modal appears showing the filename and path.

  1. Click Delete to confirm. The file is removed from your active library.

docs.title: Deleting Directories
docs.text:
To delete an entire directory, select Delete from the folder's action menu.

Recursive Deletion

Deleting a directory removes the folder and all files and subdirectories contained within it. You will be prompted to confirm the deletion before any files are touched.

docs.title: Deleting Multiple Files
docs.text:
You can delete multiple files simultaneously:

  1. Hold CTRL (or CMD) to select specific files, or SHIFT to select a continuous range of files.

  1. Right-click any selected file and choose Delete Selected Files.

  1. A confirmation modal lists all targeted files:

  1. Click Delete All to process the batch deletion.

docs.title: Soft Delete & The Trash Can
docs.text:
To protect against accidental deletions and provide a safety net for automated operations, CLU includes a configurable Trash Can system:

  • Staging location: When enabled, deleted files are moved to a temporary staging folder (/cache/trash by default) rather than being permanently destroyed on disk.
  • Automated file replacements: When resolving duplicate comics or using Find a replacement for a damaged file, the replaced file is routed to the trash, ensuring you can revert if needed.
  • Automatic eviction: In File Settings, you can configure the Max Trash Size (MB). When accumulated files exceed this threshold, the oldest items are automatically pruned.
  • Restoring files: Trashed files retain metadata pointing to their original directory path, allowing you to restore them directly back into your library if deleted by mistake.

If the Trash Can is disabled in settings, deletions are immediate and permanent.

docs.title: Move
docs.text:
Dual-Pane File Manager Interface

When the File Manager loads, it displays a dual-pane view of your storage directory in both the Source (left) and Destination (right) panels.

docs.title: Moving Files and Directories
docs.text: The dual-pane interface allows drag-and-drop transfers in either direction (Source $\rightarrow$ Destination or Destination $\rightarrow$ Source).

docs.title: Moving Files
docs.text: Navigate to the target file in one panel, then click and drag it to the desired directory in the opposing panel.

docs.title: Moving Directories
docs.text:
Navigate to the directory you wish to move, then click and drag it into its new parent folder in the opposite panel.

When moving large directories or high volumes of files, progress is reported live in the top navigation bar's Action Items indicator, allowing you to navigate away while the transfer completes in the background.

docs.title: Multi-Item Selection
docs.text:
You can select multiple files or directories simultaneously:

  • Hold SHIFT while clicking to select a contiguous range of items.
  • Hold CTRL (or CMD on macOS) while clicking to toggle individual items.

Once items are selected, you can drag the entire group to a new location at once.

docs.title: Create Folder from Files
docs.text:
When multiple comic files are selected, right-click to open the context menu and choose Create Folder with Selection:

  • Automatic series detection: If all selected files share an identical detected series name, the new folder automatically defaults to that series title.
  • Custom folder name: If selected files originate from different series or lack common naming, a prompt asks you to enter the desired folder name.

Click Create Folder to create the directory and automatically move the selected files into it.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text: CLU provides several renaming workflows in the File Manager, ranging from quick inline edits to batch string replacements and series-wide standardization.

docs.title: Rename Single Files
docs.text:
To rename an individual file or folder, hover over the item and click the :pencil2: (pencil) icon. The name turns into an active text field.

Enter the new name and press ENTER to save the change immediately to disk.

docs.title: Rename All Files in a Directory
docs.text:
In any directory listing, click the button to execute automated batch cleaning across all comic archives in that directory:

This runs the automated cleaning and formatting engine detailed in Rename All Files. Batch renames run on the shared file job queue, executing safely behind any active metadata tagging or XML removal jobs.

docs.title: Remove Text from Files
docs.text:
To remove specific characters or substrings (such as unwanted scanner tags or volume markers like " v01") across all files in a directory, click Remove Text from Filenames:

  1. Enter the exact text you want removed (including leading or trailing spaces if applicable).
  2. Click Preview to review the proposed filename transformations before applying changes.

  1. Click Execute Rename to apply the changes to disk. A summary modal confirms the number of files updated.

docs.title: Replace Text in Filenames
docs.text:
To substitute one string for another across all files in a folder (for example, correcting "Saga of the Swamp Thing" to "The Saga of the Swamp Thing"), click Replace Text:

  1. Enter the target text to find and the replacement text.
  2. Click Preview to inspect the before and after comparisons.

  1. Click Execute Rename to process the changes.

docs.title: Rename Series
docs.text:
If an entire folder of files has an incorrect, truncated, or inconsistent series prefix, click Rename Series. This operation replaces the series name across all files in the directory while preserving the existing {issue} and {year} values.

  1. Enter the desired series title.
  2. Click Preview to verify how the new series name pairs with existing issue numbers and years.

  1. Click Execute Rename to finalize the batch update.

docs.title: Split File
docs.text:
The Split File tool allows you to deconstruct omnibus archives, digital trade paperbacks, or multi-issue collections into individual, single-issue CBZ archives. This ensures each issue can be indexed, read, and matched individually within your library.

Format Support

Split File operates on CBZ archives. To split a CBR file, first convert or rebuild it as a CBZ using Convert Directory or Single File Rebuild.

docs.title: How to Split an Archive
docs.text:
1. In the File Manager, locate the multi-issue CBZ, open the per-file dropdown menu, and select Split File.
  2. CLU unpacks the archive in memory and automatically analyzes page image filenames (such as Series 003 - 0001.jpg) to detect issue boundaries.
  3. The interface opens an interactive page grid with detected groups:

Within this editor, you can:

  • Adjust boundaries: Move demarcation lines to set exactly where one issue ends and the next starts.
  • Merge or add groups: Combine erroneously split pages or manually insert boundaries that automated detection missed.

  • Set titles: Rename each detected issue prior to generating the new files.

  • Once the groupings and issue names are set, click Commit. CLU generates clean, image-only CBZ files for each issue and saves them into a new series subfolder.

docs.title: File Safety
docs.text:
Original File Preserved

Split File does not alter or overwrite the source archive. It writes separate new CBZ archives into a new series subfolder. You can inspect the resulting issues and choose whether to archive or delete the original source file.

docs.title: Folder Monitoring
docs.text:
Folder Monitoring is CLU's automated background ingestion pipeline. Running as a dedicated background worker process, it continuously watches a designated incoming directory for new comic downloads, unpacks archives, converts formats, cleans filenames, and routes processed issues directly into your library.

Whether files arrive from integrated downloaders (such as Usenet, DC++, or GetComics) or from manual transfers, Folder Monitoring automates post-processing so your comics are standardized and ready to read without manual intervention.

docs.title: Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text:
[ Incoming Downloads ]
          │
          ▼
   ┌─────────────┐
   │ WATCH Folder│ ◄── Waits for active downloads to finish (settling)
   └──────┬──────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Processing Pipeline                           │
   │  1. Auto-Unwrap nested & multipart archives   │
   │  2. Auto-Convert CBR/RAR to CBZ               │
   │  3. Auto-Extract multi-issue ZIP bundles      │
   │  4. Standardize & clean filenames             │
   └──────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
          ▼
   ┌──────────────┐
   │ TARGET Folder│ ◄── Clean, organized comics ready for reading & metadata
   └──────────────┘

docs.title: Folder Monitoring Sections
docs.text: Section Description Monitoring Setup How to enable the background monitor in Docker and configure WATCH and TARGET paths. Features & Automation Rules Extension filtering, format conversion, archive unwrapping, and pipeline integrity guards. Monitoring Logs Inspecting real-time background logs to track active file ingestion. File Processing Settings Global configuration for naming patterns, subdirectory traversal, and ignored terms.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: When Folder Monitoring is enabled, CLU applies an automated processing pipeline to any new files or directories appearing in your WATCH folder.

docs.title: Ignored Extensions
docs.text:
Folder monitoring can be configured to ignore specific file extensions. This serves two purposes:

  1. Ignoring active download temp files: File transfer tools often create temporary files while downloads are in flight. Adding these extensions ensures CLU ignores them until transfers finish.
  2. Excluding non-comic files: Prevents unwanted companion files (such as .nfo, .torrent, or raw images) from being moved or processed into your library.

Default ignored file extensions include:

.crdownload,.torrent,.tmp,.mega,.rar,.bak,.dctmp

docs.title: Renaming
docs.text: When enabled, incoming comic files are automatically cleaned and standardized using the rules described in Rename All Files. Filenames are formatted according to your configured Custom Rename Pattern as they move from WATCH to TARGET.

docs.title: Process Subdirectories
docs.text: By default, monitoring processes only files resting in the root of the WATCH directory. Enabling Process Subdirectories allows the monitor to traverse nested child folders inside WATCH, applying extraction, conversion, and renaming to all contained files.

docs.title: Move Subdirectories
docs.text: When downloading multi-issue packs or complete series runs, files often arrive inside a series subfolder. Enabling Move Subdirectories preserves this grouping: the entire subfolder is cleaned, renamed using standardized series naming rules, and moved into the TARGET directory with its issues intact.

docs.title: Auto ZIP Extraction
docs.text: When enabled, multi-file .zip packages appearing in the WATCH folder are automatically extracted once completely written to disk. Extracted files maintain their internal folder hierarchy and are subsequently processed by the remaining pipeline steps.

docs.title: Convert to CBZ
docs.text: When enabled, any .cbr or .rar comic archive detected in the WATCH folder is automatically converted into a standard .cbz archive before moving to TARGET.

docs.title: Auto-Unwrap for Hybrid & Multipart Releases
docs.text:
Usenet releases and complex web downloads often arrive as nested, multi-part, or obfuscated packages — such as a folder of .zip or .rar split volumes that extract to another archive layer before revealing the final comic file.

CLU automatically detects and unwraps these packages through a dedicated pre-processing workflow:

  1. Identifies the release folder within the WATCH directory.
  2. Waits for all parts to finish downloading (settling) before initiating extraction.
  3. Extracts nested archives layer-by-layer inside an isolated temporary workspace.
  4. Converts any extracted PDF documents into standard CBZ archives.
  5. Renames the extracted comic to a clean title and hands it off to the primary monitoring pipeline.

docs.title: Unwrapping Guarantees
docs.text:
• Isolated extraction: Files are unpacked in an isolated staging directory, never in place over your active files.
  • Safety checks: The unwrapper will not trigger if a valid, ready-to-read comic archive already exists in the top level of the folder.
  • Clean error handling: Temporary extraction artifacts are purged upon success; if an extraction fails, the source archive is preserved so it can be retried or inspected.

See Searching & Grabbing for details on how Usenet releases interact with this feature.

docs.title: Pipeline Safeguards
docs.text: Folder Monitoring includes several built-in protections to ensure library stability:

docs.title: Active Download Detection
docs.text: CLU monitors file size over time to ensure files have stopped growing before attempting to read, unpack, or move them. In-progress downloads from clients like AirDC++ or torrent applications are left alone until fully written. Orphan cleanup routines will never delete files whose size is actively changing.

docs.title: Graceful Archive Error Handling
docs.text: If an archive in the WATCH directory is corrupted or unreadable, CLU attempts extraction once, logs the failure, and moves the item to the Problem Files page under the Unpack category. The file will not loop or create duplicate numbered files on successive sweeps.

docs.title: Atomic Transfers
docs.text: Files moved from WATCH to TARGET are verified upon arrival. If a transfer is interrupted, any partial destination file is cleaned up immediately, preventing the creation of numbered duplicate copies (e.g. Comic (2).cbz) on subsequent monitoring passes.

docs.title: Clean CBR Replacement
docs.text: When converting CBR files to CBZ, CLU verifies the integrity of the generated CBZ archive before safely removing the source CBR file from disk.

docs.title: Monitoring Logs
docs.text:
When Folder Monitoring is enabled, a dedicated Monitor Logs link is available in the top navigation bar.

Monitor Logs in Navigation

The Monitor Logs view displays real-time activity for files moving through the automated ingestion pipeline.

Folder Monitoring Live Log View

docs.title: Log Message Types
docs.text:
The monitoring log details each stage of automated file ingestion:

  • Config Reloaded: The monitoring daemon checks for configuration changes and reloads dynamically without requiring a container restart.
  • Processing File: Identifies the specific file currently undergoing evaluation in the WATCH directory.
  • Waiting For: Indicates that a file is actively being written or downloaded. The monitor pauses until the file size stabilizes.
  • Renamed: Displays the original filename alongside the newly formatted name produced by the renaming engine.
  • Moved File: Reports the transfer path as processed files move from the WATCH directory to the TARGET directory.
  • Checking If: Inspects the internal file structure and extension to determine if format conversion (e.g. CBR $\rightarrow$ CBZ) is needed.
  • Sending Convert Request: Dispatches the file to the conversion worker and logs the outcome upon completion.

For general application errors and database maintenance events, refer to the main App Logs page.

docs.title: Monitoring Setup
docs.text: Folder Monitoring runs as an isolated background process to ensure continuous file processing without degrading web interface responsiveness.

docs.title: Docker Compose Configuration
docs.text:
To enable folder monitoring, ensure your docker-compose.yaml mounts a secondary volume for incoming files and sets the MONITOR=yes environment flag:

version: '3.9'
services:
    comic-utils:
        image: allaboutduncan/comic-utils-web:latest
        container_name: clu
        logging:
            driver: "json-file"
            options:
                max-size: '20m'
                max-file: '3'
        restart: always
        ports:
            - '5577:5577'
        volumes:
            - "/path/to/local/config:/config"
            - "/path/to/local/cache:/cache"
            # Main comic library (must be mapped to /data)
            - "/e/Comics:/data"
            # Secondary volume for incoming downloads
            - "/f/Downloads:/downloads"
        environment:
            - FLASK_ENV=production
            # Enable folder monitoring background process
            - MONITOR=yes

Key configuration points:

  • Secondary Volume Mount (e.g. "/f/Downloads:/downloads"): Mounts your download client's destination directory into the container.
  • MONITOR=yes: Starts the dedicated background monitoring daemon inside the container.

If you installed CLU without monitoring enabled, update your docker-compose.yaml with these values and restart the container (docker compose up -d).

docs.title: Directory Configuration (WATCH & TARGET)
docs.text:
Once monitoring is enabled, navigate to Settings > File Processing in the CLU web interface to assign your directory paths:

Folder Monitoring Configuration in Settings

  • WATCH Folder: The incoming directory monitored for new files. Download clients should deposit completed downloads here.
  • TARGET Folder: The destination directory where files are moved once unpacked, converted, and renamed. This can be your main /data library or an intermediate staging folder.

Directory Placement

Keep your WATCH folder outside /data. Storing raw incoming downloads in a separate folder prevents incomplete or temporary download files from appearing in your active comic collection.

docs.title: Library Insights
docs.text:
The Library Insights page provides a quick overview of your collection, including the number of comics, popular publishers, total file size, and more.

The Recently Read has a link to an expanded Timeline view that shows your full reading history.

Additional information about Top Writers, Top Artists, and Top Characters can be found in the Reading Trends section.

Some of these statistics are also available as JSON from the Insights API.

docs.title: Insights API
docs.text: I have made a small number of the Library Insights available as an API endpoint at /api/insights.

docs.title: Current API Data
docs.text:
{
  "issues_read": 6,
  "root_folders": 88,
  "total_files": 116205,
  "total_size": 4381449407305
}

docs.title: Homepage Widget
docs.text:
If you are using the Homepage, you can use this API to display the data in your dashboard.

    - CLU:
        icon: https://github.com/allaboutduncan/comic-utils/blob/main/static/images/clu.png?raw=true
        href: your-CLU-URL #link the widget to your CLU instance
        description: Comic Library Utilities
        widget:
            type: customapi
            url: http://your-CLU-URL/api/insights #API URL
            refreshInterval: 3600000  # optional - in milliseconds, defaults to 10s
            method: GET
            mappings:
            - field: total_files
              label: Total Files
              format: number
            - field: total_size
              label: Total Size
              format: bytes
            - field: root_folders
              label: Publishers
              format: number
            - field: issues_read
              label: Issues Read
              format: number

docs.title: Available Insights
docs.text:
The Library Insights page provides a quick overview of your collection, including the number of comics, popular publishers, total file size, and more.

Here's a quick summary of the current available insights:

docs.title: Collection Stats
docs.text:
• Total Files: This is anything that is scanned, saved to the database, and displayed in the collection view.
  • Total Size: This is the total size of all files in your collection.
  • Folders: This is the number of folders in your collection.
  • File Type Distribution: This is the number of files of each type in your collection. Clicking a file type will remove it from the chart.
  • Top Publishers: This is a list of the top 10 publishers in your collection, based on the number of comics they have.

docs.title: Reading Stats
docs.text:
The below stats can be filtered by year, by clicking the dropdown menu in the right.

  • Issues Read: This is the number of issues that you have read.
  • Total Pages Read: This is the total number of pages that you have read.
  • Total Hours Read: This is the total number of hours that you have read.
  • Reading Heatmap: This is a heatmap of the number of issues you have read month over month for each year.
  • Reading Activity: This is a daily graph of the number of issues you have read over the past 12 months.

docs.title: Reading Activity
docs.text:
• Recently Read: This is a list of the last 20 comics you have read.
    • You can click the Timeline button to open the timeline view and see your full reading history.

docs.title: Reading Trends
docs.text:
• Top Writers: This is a list of your top 10 writers, based on the number of comics you have read.
  • Top Artists: This is a list of your top 10 artists, based on the number of comics you have read.
  • Top Characters: This is a list of your top 10 characters, based on the number of comics you have read.
  • Top Publishers: This is a list of your top 10 publishers, based on the number of comics you have read.

Clicking on the name of a writer, artist, or character will open the timeline view and show you a list of all the comics in your collection matching that writer, artist, or character.

In the above example, we can see there are 852 comics by this writer with 748 published by DC Comics and 88 of them in the Green Lantern series.

docs.title: Top 20 Charts
docs.text:
• Top 20 Series: This is a list of the top 20 series in your collection, based on the number of issues they have.
  • Top 20 Largest Comics: This is a list of the top 20 comics in your collection, based on the size of the files.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
The Timeline view shows your full reading history over time.

As you scroll, your history is lazy-loaded in the background allowing you to see your entire detailed reading history in one place.

docs.title: Timeline Features
docs.text: Multiple options are available on the Timeline view.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text: Using the drop-downs and buttons at the time, you can filter your timeline to a specific Year and/or Month. You can also use the Search input to filter your timeline to see when exactly you read a specific issue or series.

docs.title: Hide or Mark as Unread
docs.text: You can now hide comics you have read from your timeline. Hidden comics will still count in your overall stats (issues read and pages read). Additional, you can also set an issue as Unread.

docs.title: Generate Montly "Wrapped" Slides
docs.text: You can generate a visual monthy summary for any month of your reading history. Simply click the Monthly Wrapped button at the top and select the options (see image above). Click Generate and you'll be presented with 2 images sized for sharing on social media or other platforms.

docs.title: Local Metadata Databases
docs.text:
Getting metadata and building ComicInfo.xml files for a large collection through an online API is slow — you're bound by rate limits and network round-trips. CLU can instead read metadata from a local SQLite database stored on your own disk, which is dramatically faster for bulk-updating a big library and has no API rate limits.

Two local databases are supported:

Database What it is Setup Grand Comics Database (GCD) A SQLite dump you download from comics.org. GCD SQLite Setup ComicVine (Local DB) A prebuilt SQLite copy of ComicVine data. ComicVine Local DB Setup

SQLite replaces MySQL in v6.0

Earlier releases required running a separate MySQL container for local GCD data. As of v6.0 that's gone — both local databases are now single SQLite files that CLU reads directly from disk. There's no separate database server, no Docker network, and no import step to run.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Both databases follow the same pattern:

  1. Download the SQLite file and place it somewhere mapped into the CLU container.
  2. In Settings → Metadata Providers, enter the file's full path in the provider's Database Path field.
  3. Save and Test — CLU reads the file directly from disk (nothing is uploaded).
  4. Enable the provider for the libraries where you want to use it.

A snapshot in time

A local database is a snapshot from the day you downloaded it — it won't contain comics released after that date. This is ideal for bulk-updating your back catalog; pair it with an online provider (Metron or the ComicVine API) to cover brand-new releases.

docs.title: ComicVine Local DB Setup
docs.text:
CLU can read ComicVine metadata from a local SQLite database instead of the ComicVine API. Because it's read straight from disk, there are no API rate limits — ideal for tagging a large library quickly.

New in v6.0

Local ComicVine (SQLite) support is new in v6.0.

New in v6.5 — CLU can fetch and update the database for you

You no longer have to download and unpack the database by hand. Point CLU at a path, click Download now, and it does the rest — and it can keep the copy current on its own from then on.

docs.title: 1. Choose a path CLU can reach
docs.text:
Pick a location that is mapped into your CLU container. If you map /config in your Docker setup, /config/comicvine.db is a good choice.

The file doesn't have to exist yet — CLU will create it. It reads the database directly from disk; nothing is uploaded.

Check you have the room first

The download is around 540 MB and unpacks to several GB — on the same volume that will hold your current copy.

Because a replacement is only swapped in once it's fully verified, peak usage is roughly old + new. Make sure the volume has room for both.

docs.title: 2. Configure the provider
docs.text:
In Settings → Metadata Providers, find the ComicVine (Local DB) card and enter the full path in the Database Path field (e.g. /config/comicvine.db).

Click Save .

Docker / headless alternative

Instead of entering the path in the UI, you can set the COMICVINE_DATABASE_PATH environment variable on your CLU container. Saved credentials take priority; the environment variable is the fallback.

docs.title: 3. Download the database
docs.text:
Under the database path field are two controls:

Control What it does Download now Fetches, unpacks and verifies the database immediately. This also works as a first download, so it's how you bootstrap a new install — there are no manual steps to do first. Keep this database up to date automatically Checks for a newer copy every 2 weeks and replaces the file at the path above.

Progress appears in Active Operations. This runs in the background because it far outlasts a web request — you can navigate away, and closing the tab doesn't cancel it.

When it finishes, click Test . On success you'll see a green Connected badge.

Automatic updates are off by default

A download and disk write of this size must not start unannounced when you upgrade CLU, so the switch ships off.

The Download now button isn't gated — clicking it is a choice you've just made.

An update is a no-op until it succeeds

Nothing replaces your database until the new file has been downloaded, unpacked, checksum-verified against the publisher's own hash, and confirmed to actually be a ComicVine database.

A failed run — a dead mirror, a truncated download, a full disk — leaves your existing file exactly where it was. You can't end up with a half-written database.

docs.title: Downloading it yourself
docs.text:
If you'd rather fetch it by hand — an air-gapped install, or you already have a copy — you still can. Grab a prebuilt ComicVine SQLite database and drop it at the path you configured above. A community-maintained copy (last updated July 16, 2026) is available here:

https://pixeldrain.com/u/YkFtSLoC

This is the fallback path, not the normal one. Download now is simpler and verifies what it fetches.

docs.title: 4. Order it above the ComicVine API
docs.text:
For the best of both worlds, order ComicVine (Local DB) above the online ComicVine provider in your library's provider priority. CLU will serve metadata from the local database first and fall back to the ComicVine API for anything the local copy is missing (such as very recent releases).

For usage while browsing, see File Management → Adding Metadata.

Fixed in v6.6 — HTML in summaries

The local database stores descriptions as HTML, which used to end up in the <Summary> field. CLU now converts them to plain text when it writes ComicInfo. Files tagged before v6.6 keep their HTML until re-tagged. See Metadata.

docs.title: GCD SQLite Setup
docs.text: The Grand Comics Database (GCD) publishes a full SQLite dump of its data. Download it once, point CLU at the file, and you have a fast, offline metadata source for bulk-tagging your collection.

docs.title: 1. Download the SQLite dump
docs.text:
You'll need a free account at the Grand Comics Database (comics.org).

Once you're registered and logged in, visit https://www.comics.org/download/ and:

  • Select Private Use
  • Download the SQLite version of the dump

It's a large file

The GCD dump is large (roughly 6 GB). CLU reads it directly from disk — it is never uploaded — so put it somewhere with room to spare.

docs.title: 2. Place the file where CLU can reach it
docs.text: Extract the download and move the .db file to a location that is mapped into your CLU container. For example, if you map /config in your Docker setup, drop the file at /config/gcd.db.

docs.title: 3. Configure the provider
docs.text:
In Settings → Metadata Providers, find the Grand Comics Database card and enter the full path to the file in the Database Path field (e.g. /config/gcd.db).

Click Save , then Test . On success you'll see a green Connected badge, and the card footer shows live counts from the database (series, issues, stories, publishers, creators).

Docker / headless alternative

Instead of entering the path in the UI, you can set the GCD_DATABASE_PATH environment variable on your CLU container. Saved credentials take priority; the environment variable is the fallback.

Missing tables

If the dump is missing tables, the provider footer warns you — credits and characters may be incomplete, or (for core tables) series/issue lookups may fail entirely. Re-download from comics.org if you see this.

docs.title: Metadata Languages (optional)
docs.text: The GCD contains entries in many languages. Use the Metadata Languages field on the provider card to restrict lookups to the languages you want, as a comma-separated list of codes (e.g. en,es,fr). The default is en. Click Save next to the field after changing it.

docs.title: 4. Enable it for your libraries
docs.text:
Enable the GCD provider for the libraries where you want to use it, and set its priority relative to your other providers.

For usage while browsing, see File Management → Adding Metadata.

docs.title: Problem Files
docs.text:
New in v6.5

The Problem Files page is new in v6.5.

Before v6.5, a damaged comic produced a generic broken tile in the grid and a line in the app log. There was no list of what was broken and no way to act on it.

Find it in the gear menu → Problem Files.

Store Owner only

Problem Files is gated exactly like Settings and Schedules — Clerks and Readers never see it, in the menu or by direct URL. See Roles & Permissions.

docs.title: An empty page does not mean your library is clean
docs.text:
This is the first thing to understand about the page, because the empty state is otherwise ambiguous.

CLU does not scan your library looking for damage. A file appears here because an operation CLU actually attempted tried to read it and could not. Nothing on this page is speculative, and nothing is a prediction.

So an empty page means nothing has failed — not your library is healthy. A comic you have never opened, never rebuilt and never re-tagged could be thoroughly corrupt and will not appear here until something touches it.

To find damage before something trips over it, turn on the library health scan.

docs.title: Library health scan
docs.text:
New in v6.8

The library health scan is new in v6.8. It is off by default.

The health scan opens every comic to check that it can be read. It also finds orphaned files, empty folders, series.json problems and duplicates. Anything it finds lands on this page alongside the other rows.

It's controlled from the Library health card at the top of the page:

Control What it does Scan automatically Turns the scheduled scan on. Off by default. Every How often it runs: every hour, 6 hours (the default), 12 hours, day or week. Files per run How many comics each run checks: 50, 200 (the default), 500, 1000 or 2500. Run scan now Checks the next batch right away, plus series.json, stray files, empty folders and ComicInfo counts. Review duplicates Opens the Duplicates page. The badge shows how many groups are open.

docs.title: How it works through a library
docs.text:
The scan is rolling. Each run checks one batch of files, the ones checked longest ago first, so a large library is covered over several runs rather than one long one. Once every file has been read, files are re-checked periodically.

The cheaper folder-wide checks (series.json, stray files and empty folders) run at most once a day on the schedule. Run scan now always includes them.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: The coverage bar shows the share of the library with a current result: 40% checked means 60% unknown, not 60% healthy. A file that changes on disk (a new size or modified time) counts as unchecked again until the scan reads it.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
The card's score starts at 100/100, and loses points for damaged files, duplicate groups, orphans and other problems. It shows red when any file is damaged, amber for anything else below 100, and green at 100.

Before the first scan, the status line reminds you: an empty list below means nothing has failed, not that the library is clean.

From Guided Setup

The Library Health step of Guided Setup sets the same switch and interval, and can run a scan for you. It accepts any interval from 1 to 168 hours.

docs.title: Where a row came from
docs.text:
Every row records which operation hit the error, and that tells you what CLU was doing at the time.

Source What was being attempted Thumbnail Generating the cover for the grid. Rebuild A single-file or directory rebuild. Metadata write Writing ComicInfo.xml back into the archive. CBR conversion A CBR/RAR that wouldn't convert to CBZ. Unpack An archive in your WATCH folder that wouldn't open.

Unpack is the odd one out

An Unpack row's path is a download, not a library comic. The file never reached your library at all — which is exactly why nothing else would ever have told you about it.

This is the row type that explains "my download vanished and never appeared in the library". See Folder Monitoring → Features.

docs.title: One file can appear twice
docs.text:
Rows are keyed on the file and the source. A comic whose thumbnail fails and whose rebuild fails is two rows, tracked independently — fixing or dismissing one does not clear the other.

That's deliberate: the two failures can have different causes, and a thumbnail that can't be written because of a cache permissions problem says nothing at all about the archive.

docs.title: Filtering the list
docs.text: Filter What it does Source pills Show only rows from one operation — Thumbnail, Rebuild, Metadata write, CBR conversion, Unpack. Path filter Narrows the list to paths matching what you type. Useful for checking a single series or a single mount. Show dismissed Brings dismissed rows back into view. Off by default.

docs.title: What you can do about a row
docs.text: Action What it does Details Shows the archive error in full, exactly as the library reported it. Retry Thumbnail rows only. Re-attempts the thumbnail immediately and synchronously, so you see the result straight away. Rebuild Unpacks the archive and repacks it as a fresh CBZ. Find a replacement Opens the source search, pre-filled from the filename. See Replacing a damaged file. Dismiss Hides the row until the file changes on disk. Delete Moves the file to the trash. Remove Forgets the row without touching the file.

docs.title: Rebuild
docs.text:
Rebuild is honest about its odds

Rebuild's only real repair is an archive that's a RAR wearing a .cbz name. Repacking fixes the container; it cannot invent bytes that aren't there.

A genuine CRC error aborts the whole extraction, so for most real damage a rebuild will fail the same way the original operation did. That's why the page demotes Rebuild and promotes Find a replacement on those rows.

The button placement is a recommendation, not a limitation — Rebuild is still there, and it's still worth one click if you're not sure which kind of problem you have.

docs.title: Dismiss
docs.text:
Dismiss is keyed to the file, not the message

A dismissal lifts by itself if the file is rewritten on disk and still fails. You don't have to remember to un-dismiss anything.

It deliberately does not match on the error text, because a damaged archive raises a different error depending on which page happens to be read first — so matching on the message would let the same broken comic come back as a "new" problem over and over.

docs.title: Unreachable rows
docs.text:
If a library is unmounted — a sleeping NAS, a disconnected share — its rows come back marked unreachable, and Remove is the only action offered.

CLU deliberately won't prune rows it can't positively prove are gone. A mount that's simply asleep would otherwise empty the page overnight and take the record of every real problem with it.

docs.title: An unwritable cache is not a damaged comic
docs.text:
When the failure is CLU's own /cache

Some thumbnail failures aren't about the archive at all — the comic reads fine and CLU can't write the result, usually because /cache has the wrong ownership or is mounted read-only.

The page says so explicitly on those rows and hides Delete entirely. It is the one case where the fix is a permissions change rather than a replacement, and deleting a perfectly good comic would be exactly the wrong move.

Check your /cache volume mapping and your PUID/PGID. See Quickstart.

docs.title: The page caps at 2,000 open rows
docs.text:
A mount whose permissions are revoked mid-scan turns every file in it into an error. A 40,000-row page helps nobody and takes a long time to load, so CLU stops recording new open rows at 2,000.

If you hit the cap, the problem is almost certainly one shared cause — a mount, a permissions change, a full disk — rather than 2,000 individually broken comics. Fix the cause and clear the rows.

docs.text:
• Duplicates — review the duplicate groups the health scan finds.
  • Replacing a damaged file — download a clean copy straight onto the damaged file's own path.
  • Single File Rebuild — what Rebuild does, and what happens when it fails.
  • Folder Monitoring → Features — where Unpack rows come from.

docs.title: Duplicates
docs.text:
New in v6.8

The Duplicate Files page is new in v6.8.

The library health scan groups copies of the same comic. The Duplicate Files page is where you review those groups: pick the copy to keep, and send the rest to the trash.

Find it from Problem Files with the Review duplicates button, or from the Library Health in Guided Setup.

Store Owner only

Like Problem Files, the Duplicates page is Store Owner only.

docs.title: Exact and likely groups
docs.text:
Group Why it's grouped How sure Exact Identical files (same content hash). The files are byte-for-byte identical. Certain. Likely Tagged as the same series, issue and year, with matching file names, or same name in one folder, apart from a copy marker (Comic (1).cbz next to Comic.cbz). Check before you trash. A variant cover or a different scan can match on tags.

Each group shows how much space you'd get back by keeping one copy.

Only checked files can be exact duplicates

The scan works through the library a batch at a time, and a file can only join an exact group once the scan has read it. On a large library the list fills in over several runs. An empty page means no duplicates among the files checked so far. The coverage figure on Problem Files shows how far the scan has got.

docs.title: Picking the copy to keep
docs.text:
Each file in a group is listed with its folder, size and modified date, plus badges for Damaged, Tagged or No ComicInfo, and the metadata provider.

CLU pre-selects a keeper, preferring a copy that is, in order:

  1. Not damaged
  2. Tagged with ComicInfo.xml
  3. A .cbz
  4. Larger
  5. Newer

Change the Keep button if you'd rather keep a different one.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action What it does Compare For a pair, a read-only side-by-side view of tags, pages and file details. Keep selected, trash the rest Asks you to confirm, listing what is kept and what is trashed, then moves the others to the trash. You can restore them from there. Dismiss Hides the group until the next health scan. It comes back if that scan still finds it. Not duplicates Hides the group for good. It comes back only if another copy turns up. Restore Turn on Show dismissed to see hidden groups, labelled Dismissed until next scan or Marked not duplicates, and restore one.

Nothing is removed unless you choose a copy to keep. Before trashing, CLU checks again that the group hasn't changed. If a new copy has appeared since the page loaded, you get a Group changed message: reload and review the group again.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Problem Files: the health scan, coverage and damaged files.
  • Delete: how the trash works.

docs.title: Replacing a damaged file
docs.text:
New in v6.5

Find a replacement is new in v6.5, and is reached from a row on the Problem Files page.

For most real archive damage, Rebuild can't help — the bytes are gone. What you actually want is a clean copy of the same issue, filed in the same place, with the damaged one taken away. That's what this does.

docs.title: Why this had to be built
docs.text:
CLU's normal import only files issues that are missing. A corrupt file is still a file, so an ordinary download of the same issue would be matched against a slot that is already occupied, and the replacement would sit in your processed folder forever while the broken copy stayed in your library.

Find a replacement breaks that tie: the download is claimed for the damaged file's own path from the moment you queue it.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
1. Search. Click Find a replacement on a Problem Files row. The source search opens pre-filled from the filename, querying every configured source.
  2. Queue a download. Pick a result as you normally would.
  3. CLU claims it for that path. The queued download is bound to the damaged file, not just to the series.
  4. When it lands, CLU verifies it — see below.
  5. The swap. The damaged copy goes to the trash and the replacement moves into its place, taking its name.
  6. A banner on the Problem Files page reports the result until you dismiss it.

docs.title: What you'll see while it runs
docs.text: State What you'll see What to do Claimed A download has been queued and bound to this file. Nothing — wait for it to land. Applied The swap completed. The damaged file is in the trash and the row is gone. Nothing. Empty the trash when you're happy. Failed Verification failed, or the move couldn't complete. Nothing was changed. Run Find a replacement again and pick a different release. Held The download arrived in a format that can't replace the original yet — see below. Nothing. The swap happens on a later pass.

docs.title: The replacement is checked before anything is destroyed
docs.text:
A failed verification is a no-op

Before anything moves, the downloaded file is CRC-checked end to end and must actually contain pages. A zero-page archive, a truncated download, or an HTML error page saved with a .cbz name all fail here.

A partly-readable original is worth more than a broken replacement, so if verification fails, nothing moves. The damaged file stays exactly where it is and the row stays on the page.

The damaged file goes to the trash, never straight to deletion — and if the swap fails part-way through, CLU puts it back. You can undo this yourself if you change your mind.

docs.title: A CBR won't replace a CBZ
docs.text:
That's a hold, not a failure

If the replacement arrives as a CBR and the file it's replacing is a CBZ, the swap doesn't happen yet. This is recorded as a hold, not an error — it means the conversion pipeline hasn't reached the file yet. The swap happens on a later pass, once it's a CBZ.

The reverse is allowed: a CBZ replacing a damaged CBR is an upgrade, and goes through immediately.

docs.title: You don't have to sit on the page
docs.text:
The swap is also applied by the normal download sweep, so closing the tab doesn't strand anything — the replacement will still be applied when it arrives.

The banner is the only place the result is reported, though, because a successful swap deletes the Problem Files row it came from. If you navigate away and come back to a page with one fewer row, that's what happened.

docs.title: A failed swap stops retrying
docs.text:
Deliberately

If a replacement fails verification, CLU does not try that download again, and does not keep trying nightly.

Retrying the same bad release every night would produce the same bad file every night. Run Find a replacement again and pick a different release instead.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:

  • Click to Download → The Search Modal — the search window that opens.
  • Download Status Page — where the replacement download itself appears while it runs.

docs.title: Pull List and Series Management
docs.text: CLU features an integrated Pull List and series tracking system powered by the Metron database. Similar to a pull list at a local comic book shop, it lets you subscribe to ongoing series, track weekly release schedules, identify missing back-catalogue issues, and coordinate automated downloads.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Weekly Releases: Browse current, past, and upcoming releases, filter by publisher, and subscribe in one click.
  • Series Management: Map series to local folders, manage custom naming patterns, and reconcile owned versus missing issues.
  • Automated Downloads: Feed missing issues directly into GetComics, Usenet, and DC++ download sweeps.
  • Library Automap: Scan existing sidecars (series.json and cvinfo) to import your entire library to the Pull List in a single pass.

docs.title: Pull List Sections
docs.text: Section Description Documentation Releases Browse weekly release schedules with live publisher filter pills and deep-linkable URLs. Releases Series Manage series subscriptions, folder mapping, and issue-level statuses. Series Pull List Central dashboard showing collection health color-coding and bulk monitoring toggles. Pull List Wanted Track missing back-catalogue issues and upcoming releases with integrated download searching. Wanted Weekly Packs Automate weekly bulk publisher pack downloads (Marvel, DC, Image, Dark Horse, Indie). Weekly Packs Series Search Search the Metron catalog by keyword to subscribe to new or ongoing series. Series Search Publishers Manage publisher directory paths and view provider-linked publisher records. Publishers Automap Scan existing library folders and sidecars to rapidly populate your Pull List. Automap (Scan Library)

docs.title: Metron API Configuration
docs.text:
The Pull List relies on the Metron comic database for release calendars, issue checklists, and creator metadata.

To enable Pull List features, register for a free account at Metron and enter your credentials in Settings > Metadata Providers.

docs.title: Automap (Scan Library)
docs.text: If you have an existing comic collection, adding titles to the Pull List one by one is time-consuming. Scan Library automatically inspects the sidecar files already present across your storage directories, resolves each to a verified Metron or ComicVine series, and populates your Pull List in a single batch pass.

docs.title: How Automap Works
docs.text:
1. Scans your configured library directories for series.json and cvinfo sidecar files (such as those generated by Mylar3 or earlier CLU passes).
  2. Queries Metron (and ComicVine) to resolve each sidecar to an official series ID.
  3. Groups every scanned directory into one of three classifications:

docs.title: Classification Categories
docs.text: Classification Meaning Action Required Auto CLU resolved the sidecar to a single, confident series match. None. Mapped automatically upon commit. Needs review A probable match was found, but requires user confirmation (e.g. multiple candidate volumes or fuzzy naming). Confirm or select the correct volume in the review modal. Skipped No usable sidecar or matching provider record was found. Review the displayed reason; map manually later if desired.

docs.title: The Review Workflow
docs.text:
Directories marked Needs review are presented in an interactive review modal. For each item, select the correct series volume (or accept CLU's suggestion) before applying:

Guided Setup Integration

The Pull List Scan step during Guided Setup runs this exact scan. Review candidate matches promptly, as temporary scan sessions expire after 15 minutes.

When you commit the mappings, CLU executes the following background tasks:

  • Backfills sidecars: Writes updated series.json and cvinfo files so each folder retains permanent series identification.
  • Synchronizes checklists: Queries the provider in the background to retrieve full issue lists, publication dates, and creator credits.
  • Reconciles collection: Scans local files to record which issues you already own versus which are wanted.

docs.title: Import Safeguards & Behavior
docs.text:
• ComicVine fallback: Series that exist exclusively on ComicVine are fully supported and mapped cleanly.
  • Preserves existing metadata: Existing sidecar publisher and status values are preserved rather than overwritten.
  • Mylar folder structures: Standard Mylar volume folder layouts (such as <publisher>/<series>/v<year>/) are parsed accurately without mistaking the v<year> folder for the series title.
  • Intelligent monitoring defaults: Fully collected series with an ended publication status (Cancelled or Completed) default to Not Monitored, preventing unnecessary search queries for finished runs.

docs.title: Scanning a Single Folder
docs.text:
To apply this same identification process to a single directory rather than running a full library sweep, select Add to Pull List from any series folder's action menu in the File Manager or Collection view.

Single-folder mapping runs the identical resolution pipeline: sidecars are created, checklists are synced, and owned counts are tallied. If a sidecar is missing or unreadable, a Metron search picker opens directly so you can select the correct title.

See Additional Features for detailed outcome codes.

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text:
• Pull List — Managing your subscribed series and collection health.
  • Import from Mylar3 — Migrating a Mylar3 watchlist from database and config files.
  • Series Page — Managing individual series checklists and mapping paths.

docs.title: Publishers
docs.text: The Publishers table manages publisher records registered within your Pull List system. When you subscribe to a series, CLU automatically links the publisher to its official Metron publisher record and assigns its storage directory.

docs.title: Publisher Table Fields
docs.text: Field Description ID The unique publisher identifier from the Metron database. Name The canonical publisher name (e.g. Marvel, DC Comics, Image). Path The local storage directory assigned to this publisher. Favorite Indicates whether the publisher is pinned as a favorite on the collection dashboard. Created At Timestamp recording when the publisher was registered in CLU. Actions Edit the publisher's assigned directory path or delete the publisher record.

docs.title: Editing Publisher Paths
docs.text:
Click the edit button on any publisher row to open the edit dialog:

You can modify the display name or update the mapped storage directory. Updating the path ensures future series subscribed under that publisher are filed into the correct directory location.

docs.title: Pull List
docs.text: The Pull List serves as your central subscription manager, providing an overview of every tracked series, its collection health, issue counts, and monitoring status.

docs.title: Filtering and Sorting
docs.text: The Pull List table includes fast search and sorting controls to help manage large libraries:

docs.title: Filter Options
docs.text: Filter Description Search Box Live filters series titles by keyword as you type. Publisher Dropdown menu to isolate series from a specific publisher. A–Z Bar Quick letter jump bar to filter titles alphabetically. Status Filter Filters by collection state (Complete, Missing, or Upcoming).

docs.title: Sorting Columns
docs.text:
Click any column header to toggle ascending or descending sort order:

  • Series: Alphabetical sort by title.
  • Publisher: Group series by publisher name.
  • Status: Sort by collection completeness.
  • Issues: Sort by total issue count.
  • Last Synced: Order by the date CLU last verified records against Metron.

Clicking any series title opens its dedicated Series page to manage issues and paths.

docs.title: Monitoring Status
docs.text:
Each series has a Monitor toggle:

  • Monitored: Missing issues appear on the Wanted page and are actively queried during nightly automated downloader sweeps.
  • Not Monitored: The series row is greyed out, and automated downloader queries are disabled.

Turn off monitoring for completed runs where you already have every issue or when missing issues are unavailable.

docs.title: Collection Health Color-Coding
docs.text:
Rows are color-coded based on their collection status:

Status Meaning Complete You own every currently released issue of the series. Missing One or more released issues are missing from your collection. Upcoming You own all released issues, and future issues are scheduled with upcoming store dates.

Colors adapt to your selected user theme. Use the on-page legend as a quick reference.

docs.title: Bulk Actions
docs.text:
You can apply status updates across multiple series at once using the multi-select checkboxes:

  • Select single series: Click the checkbox next to the title.
  • Select range: Click the first checkbox, then hold SHIFT and click a second checkbox.
  • Toggle individual series: Hold CTRL (or CMD on macOS) while clicking checkboxes.

Once rows are selected, use the bulk action toolbar to switch all selected series to Monitored or Not Monitored in a single click.

docs.title: Import Defaults
docs.text:
When importing series in bulk via Scan Library, monitoring flags are initialized conservatively:

  • Series that are both fully owned and have an ended publication status (Cancelled or Completed) default to Not Monitored to prevent unnecessary search requests for finished runs.
  • Series with uncollected issues or active publication runs default to Monitored.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
The Releases page displays comic books scheduled for publication during a given week, based on data from the Metron comic database.

Clicking any comic in the release grid opens the series detail view, where you can:

  • Subscribe to the series to add it to your Pull List.
  • Map to an existing directory or update its storage path.
  • Check for new issues or scan local folders for recently added files.
  • Manage monitoring status for automated downloader sweeps.

docs.title: Navigating Release Weeks
docs.text: Use the navigation arrows at the top of the page to move between past, current, and upcoming release weeks.

docs.title: Publisher Filter
docs.text:
Interactive publisher filter pills above the grid display real-time issue counts for each publisher releasing books that week:

Publisher filter pills with live counts. Selections mirror into the URL.

Click any publisher pill to isolate releases from that publisher. Because filtering runs client-side in the browser, switching between publishers is instantaneous and requires no page reloads or additional API calls.

docs.title: Deep-Linkable Filter URLs
docs.text: Your selected publisher filter is automatically mirrored into the browser URL as a query parameter (e.g. ?publisher=Marvel). This allows you to bookmark specific publisher views or use your browser's back and forward buttons to cycle through previous filter states.

docs.title: The list fills in as you watch
docs.text:
When viewing a release week for the first time (a "cold" week), the publisher pills populate progressively over your initial visits rather than appearing all at once.

Metron's weekly issue endpoint returns issue objects that associate with a series but omit the parent publisher name. Querying publishers individually for every release would require roughly 150 API calls per week, quickly consuming your daily Metron API quota.

To prevent rate-limit exhaustion, CLU utilizes a self-warming cache:

  1. A background worker queries Metron using server-side publisher filters to resolve major publishers in bulk with single requests.
  2. Capped individual lookups are performed for remaining independent and small-press titles.
  3. Newly discovered publishers are added to subsequent bulk passes, converging on a complete publisher list within a few passes.

Once a week's publisher records are cached locally, filter pills render instantly on every subsequent visit.

docs.title: Series Search
docs.text: The Series Search tool allows you to query the Metron comic database by title to find series checklists, review issue runs, and subscribe to titles.

docs.title: Searching for a Series
docs.text:
1. Type the series title in the search input.
  2. Click the Search button or press ENTER.
  3. CLU queries Metron and returns matching series records, displaying publication years, publisher names, and total issue counts.

docs.title: Filtering Results
docs.text: If a query returns multiple series with similar names or multiple volumes across years, use the Filter Results field to quickly narrow down the results list.

docs.title: Subscribing or Mapping
docs.text: Clicking on any series in the results list opens its full Series page, where you can subscribe to the title, map it to an existing storage directory, or view its issue checklist.

docs.title: Series
docs.text: The Series page displays the complete checklist and metadata for a selected series from the Metron database. From this view, you can manage your subscription, map directory paths, and control tracking status.

docs.title: Subscribing to a Series
docs.text: When viewing a series you are not currently tracking, two primary actions are available:

docs.title: Subscribe
docs.text:
Clicking Subscribe prompts you for the storage path where issues of this series will be saved.

The proposed path defaults to your configured Custom Move Pattern in File Settings. You can customize this path as needed:

Common Folder Patterns

Standard series typically use: /{Publisher}/{Series} ({Year})/

Multi-volume series can be organized using volume subfolders: /{Publisher}/{Series}/v{Year}/

Click Create & Map to create the directory (if it does not already exist), register the subscription, and create a persistent .cvinfo / series.json sidecar.

docs.title: Map Location
docs.text:
If you already have a folder containing issues of this series, click Map Location to link the subscription to that existing directory.

Navigate to the folder and click Select This Folder (or the checkmark icon). CLU scans the directory, matches your existing files against the checklist, and updates your owned count.

docs.title: Managing Active Subscriptions
docs.text: For subscribed series, the header toolbar provides the following actions:

docs.title: Remove
docs.text: Click Remove to unsubscribe from the series and remove it from your Pull List. Your local comic files are left untouched.

docs.title: Change Location
